about: Chemistry Cat is a fluffy white cat wearing round black glasses and a red bow tie, posed at a lab bench in front of a chalkboard full of formulas and doodles of cheese and milk. Beakers of colored liquid and a notepad sit in front of it, like a professor about to start a lecture. The cat is an advice animal for science puns, especially plays on element names, chemical symbols and textbook laws. The joke is the corny pun delivered with the cat's very serious academic look, so the groan is part of the fun.
origin: The photo of the bespectacled cat was turned into a pun-based advice animal in 2011 and became a favorite with students and science teachers.
usage:
Use the two boxes as a classic setup and punchline. The top box sets up the pun ("I'd tell you a chemistry joke") and the bottom box springs it ("but all the good ones argon"). It works the same way for programming, math and physics puns.

Element puns are the native format: argon, sodium, copper, helium, barium. Puns that need a bit of school knowledge to get are ideal, because the nerdy payoff is the point. Keep the setup straight-faced like the cat.
